# Rule reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_rules_doc.py from the rule registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every rule has an id, a default severity, the reason it exists, how to fix a finding and a link to the primary source. Run `guardrails explain <ID>` for the same text in a terminal.

> These rules are engineering heuristics that make a person look before content ships. They are not legal advice and passing them does not make copy compliant.

## Pack: aeo-seo

Structure checks for articles that should rank and be quoted by AI answers.

### GR-SEO-001

**Answer in the first 50 to 70 words** (warn, content rule, applies to: markdown, html)

Search features and AI answer engines lift a short, self-contained passage that answers the query. Articles that open with scene-setting push the answer below the part that gets extracted. The opening paragraph should be a direct answer that is complete by word 70.

**Fix:** Rewrite the first paragraph as a direct, declarative answer of roughly 50 to 70 words, then expand below it.

**Source:** <https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `answer_min_words` | `25` | Opening paragraphs shorter than this are too thin to stand alone. |
| `answer_max_words` | `70` | The answer must be complete within this many words. |
| `filler_openers` | `["in today's", "in this article", "in this post", "have you ever", "welcome t...` | Openings that delay the answer. |

### GR-SEO-002

**Focus keyword in title, H1, first paragraph and meta description** (warn, content rule, applies to: markdown, html)

The title link, the main heading, the opening paragraph and the meta description are the places a search engine and a reader use to decide what a page is about. A declared focus keyword that is missing from any of them usually means the brief and the copy drifted apart.

**Fix:** Use the exact focus keyword in each listed place, or change the declared keyword (front matter focus_keyword, or <meta name="focus-keyword">).

**Source:** <https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/seo-starter-guide>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `require_in` | `["title", "h1", "first_paragraph", "meta_description"]` | Places the keyword must appear: title, h1, first_paragraph, meta_description, h2. |
| `require_keyword` | `false` | Report articles that declare no focus keyword at all. |

### GR-SEO-003

**FAQ section without matching FAQPage JSON-LD** (warn, content rule, applies to: markdown, html)

An FAQ section is the easiest content for answer engines to quote, and FAQPage structured data states the question and answer pairs explicitly. The markup must describe questions that are visible on the page; questions that drift between the two are a structured data quality problem.

**Fix:** Add a <script type="application/ld+json"> FAQPage block whose mainEntity names match the visible FAQ questions one to one.

**Source:** <https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/faqpage>

### GR-SEO-004

**Image without alt text** (error, content rule, applies to: markdown, html)

WCAG success criterion 1.1.1 requires a text alternative for every non-text content. Alt text is also what image search and AI models read, so a descriptive alternative helps the image itself rank.

**Fix:** Add alt text that describes what the image shows; use alt="" only for purely decorative images.

**Source:** <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/non-text-content.html>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_empty_alt` | `true` | Accept alt="" on HTML images as an explicit decorative marker. |
| `min_alt_words` | `0` | Warn when alt text has fewer words than this (0 disables). |

### GR-SEO-005

**target=_blank link without rel="noopener"** (warn, content rule, applies to: markdown, html)

A page opened with target=_blank can reach back to the opener through window.opener unless the link carries noopener (or noreferrer). Modern browsers default to noopener, but older ones and some embedded webviews do not, and many house styles require the attribute on every external link.

**Fix:** Add rel="noopener" to every link that opens a new tab.

**Source:** <https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#link-type-noopener>

## Pack: deploy-safety

Action rules that stop agents from changing production directly (PreToolUse).

### GR-DEP-001

**Direct write to a protected host or path** (error, action rule, applies to: Bash)

An agent that can reach a production server will eventually fix something there directly: an scp of one file, a sed -i over ssh. The change skips review, the repository drifts from what is live, and the next deploy silently reverts it. Changes to protected targets go through a pull request.

**Fix:** Change the source in the repository on a branch, open a pull request and let the merge deploy it.

**Source:** <https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `override` | `"GUARDRAILS_OVERRIDE=1"` | Token that lets an emergency command through. Empty disables overrides. |
| `instead` | `"Make the change on a branch and open a pull request; let the reviewed merge ...` | What the agent is told to do instead. |
| `protected_hosts` | `[]` | Hostnames (or ssh aliases) that only a reviewed deploy may write to. |
| `protected_paths` | `[]` | Absolute paths (remote docroots or local mounts) that only a deploy may write to. |

### GR-DEP-002

**Edit to a protected file** (error, action rule, applies to: Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit)

Some files must never be edited by hand: a mounted production docroot, generated bundles, vendored code, deploy workflows. An agent editing them directly bypasses the pipeline that owns them.

**Fix:** Edit the source the file is built or deployed from, on a branch, and open a pull request.

**Source:** <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `override` | `"GUARDRAILS_OVERRIDE=1"` | Token that lets an emergency command through. Empty disables overrides. |
| `instead` | `"Make the change on a branch and open a pull request; let the reviewed merge ...` | What the agent is told to do instead. |
| `protected_paths` | `[]` | Absolute paths that only a deploy may write to. |
| `protected_globs` | `[]` | Globs, relative to the config file, for files agents must not edit. |

### GR-DEP-003

**Push straight to a protected branch** (error, action rule, applies to: Bash)

Force pushing rewrites shared history, and pushing directly to the deploy branch skips review. When the merge to main is what deploys, an agent's direct push is a production change nobody reviewed.

**Fix:** Push a feature branch and open a pull request; never force push a protected branch.

**Source:** <https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `override` | `"GUARDRAILS_OVERRIDE=1"` | Token that lets an emergency command through. Empty disables overrides. |
| `instead` | `"Make the change on a branch and open a pull request; let the reviewed merge ...` | What the agent is told to do instead. |
| `protected_branches` | `["main", "master", "production"]` | Branches only a reviewed merge may update. |
| `block_direct_push` | `false` | Also block non-force pushes to protected branches. |

## Pack: eu-marketing

Consumer-protection patterns for EU-facing marketing copy.

### GR-EU-001

**Conditional 'free' claim** (error, content rule, applies to: markdown, html, text)

Under Annex I point 20 of the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, describing a product as 'free', 'gratis' or 'without charge' when the customer has to pay anything beyond the unavoidable cost of responding is one of the practices that are unfair in all circumstances: no case-by-case test applies. AI-written offers like a no-cost website paid back through a hosting plan are the classic trap.

**Fix:** Describe what is actually covered ('we cover 100% of the design and development cost') and state the recurring price in the same sentence with equal prominence.

**Source:** <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition_markers` | `["per month", "/month", "/mo", "a month", "monthly", "per year", "/year", "/y...` | Words that turn 'free' into a conditional offer when they appear in the same passage. |
| `allowed_phrases` | `["feel free", "free software", "free and open source", "free/libre", "free sp...` | Phrases where 'free' is not a price claim. |
| `currencies` | `["\u20ac", "EUR", "euro", "euros"]` | A price in the passage also counts as a condition. |
| `window` | `240` | How many characters around 'free' to search, within the same paragraph. |
| `flag_unconditional` | `false` | Also warn on 'free' with no condition nearby. |

### GR-EU-002

**Price without a VAT-inclusive figure** (error, content rule, applies to: markdown, html, text)

The Price Indication Directive requires the selling price shown to consumers to be the final price including VAT and all other taxes. A net price can appear, but only next to the VAT-inclusive figure. Copy written for B2B buyers is often reused on consumer pages without the gross figure.

**Fix:** Add the VAT-inclusive figure next to the price, for example '15 euro (18.60 euro incl. VAT)'.

**Source:** <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/1998/6/oj>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vat_rate` | `24` | VAT rate used to suggest and check the inclusive figure, as a percent (24) or fraction (0.24). |
| `currencies` | `["\u20ac", "EUR", "euro", "euros"]` | Currency symbols and words that mark a price. |
| `inclusive_markers` | `["incl. VAT", "incl VAT", "including VAT", "inc. VAT", "inc VAT", "VAT includ...` | Phrases that mark a figure as VAT-inclusive. |
| `exclusive_markers` | `["excl. VAT", "excl VAT", "excluding VAT", "ex. VAT", "ex VAT", "+ VAT", "plu...` | Phrases that mark a figure as net of VAT. |
| `window` | `160` | How many characters around a price to look for the VAT figure, within the same paragraph. |

### GR-EU-003

**Uptime SLA, guarantee or 24/7 wording** (error, content rule, applies to: markdown, html, text)

Promises like '99.9% uptime', 'guaranteed results' or '24/7 support' are claims a trader must be able to honour. A misleading claim about the nature or availability of a service is a misleading action under Article 6 of the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, and a sales page that promises more than the contract creates liability the terms of service try to exclude.

**Fix:** Describe what you actually do ('we monitor the site and respond during business hours') and keep service levels in the contract, not in marketing copy.

**Source:** <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowed_phrases` | `[]` | Exact phrases to allow, for example a product name that contains 'guarantee'. |
| `extra_patterns` | `[]` | Additional regular expressions to flag. |

### GR-EU-004

**Client name or logo without a consent record** (error, content rule, applies to: markdown, html, text)

Showing a client's name or logo implies an endorsement. Claiming approval or endorsement that was not given is a blacklisted practice (Annex I point 4 of the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive), and naming individuals needs a lawful basis under the GDPR. Agents happily reuse names from case notes, so every name on a watch list must have a written consent record before it is published.

**Fix:** Get written consent, add the name to the consent registry with the date and where the consent lives, or anonymise the reference ('a bakery in Lyon').

**Source:** <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `watch_names` | `[]` | Client names to watch for. Nothing is flagged until you list names here. |
| `consent_registry` | `"consent/approved.txt"` | File of approved names, relative to the config file. |

## Pack: house-style

Characters and words your brand never ships.

### GR-STY-001

**Banned character** (error, content rule, applies to: markdown, html, text)

Some characters are a tell. AI-drafted copy leans on the em dash, so a house rule against it keeps copy from reading as machine-written, and one config line bans any other character your style guide rules out.

**Fix:** Use a comma, a period, a colon or a plain hyphen instead.

**Source:** <https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U2000.pdf>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `banned_chars` | `["\u2014", "\u2013"]` | Characters that must not appear in prose. |
| `exempt_quotes` | `true` | Skip text inside quotation marks, <q> and <blockquote>: never edit a quote. |

### GR-STY-002

**Banned word or phrase** (warn, content rule, applies to: markdown, html, text)

Every brand has words it does not use: inflated claims, jargon, competitor names or phrases that mark copy as generic. Listing them once in config stops every agent from reintroducing them.

**Fix:** Replace the phrase with the suggested wording, or rewrite the sentence in plain words.

**Source:** <https://developers.google.com/style/word-list>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `banned_words` | `[]` | Phrases to flag, optionally 'phrase => suggestion'. Case-insensitive, whole words. |
| `exempt_quotes` | `true` | Skip text inside quotation marks, <q> and <blockquote>. |

## Pack: secrets

Credentials that must never be written into content, config or code.

### GR-SEC-001

**Provider API key or token** (error, content rule, applies to: *)

Agents paste credentials wherever the conversation already is: a draft article, a config file, a commit. Provider tokens have documented shapes (AWS, GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI, Stripe, Slack, Google), so they can be stopped before they are written, not after they are pushed.

**Fix:** Remove the value, load it from an environment variable or a secrets manager, and rotate the key.

**Source:** <https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allow_patterns` | `[]` | Regular expressions for values that are known test fixtures. |

### GR-SEC-002

**Private key block** (error, content rule, applies to: *)

A PEM or OpenSSH private key in a repository or a page gives anyone who reads it the identity the key stands for: a server login, a signing key or a TLS certificate.

**Fix:** Delete the key from the file and its history, store it outside the repository and issue a new key.

**Source:** <https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html>

### GR-SEC-003

**Hard-coded secret assignment** (warn, content rule, applies to: *)

Not every credential has a known prefix. A random-looking value assigned to a name like token, secret or password is usually a hard-coded credential (CWE-798).

**Fix:** Read the value from the environment or a secrets manager; if it is a fixture, add it to allow_patterns.

**Source:** <https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html>

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `min_entropy` | `3.5` | Minimum Shannon entropy (bits per character) for a value to count as random. |
| `key_names` | `["api_key", "apikey", "api-key", "secret", "secret_key", "client_secret", "to...` | Names that mark an assignment as a credential. |
| `allow_patterns` | `[]` | Regular expressions for values that are known fixtures. |
